quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — CPO LASER READINESS, CEO Jim Anderson, asked about the CPO laser revenue expected in fiscal Q2: 'we have already started production wafers for those shipments in our December quarter, and that customer continues to tell us to please ship more as fast as possible.' He called the design 'outstanding' with 'some significant technical advantages and production advantages', and stressed the content beyond the laser: 'We supply lasers, external laser modules, the different optical connectors, the fiber optic cable, the fiber attach unit.'

CALL (verbatim) — LTA PRICING AND THE PATH TO A $3 BILLION QUARTER, CEO Jim Anderson: LTAs 'almost always have not just a volume commitment, but agreed-upon pricing as well. The pricing is set for, I think, all or almost all of our LTAs out through the length of the LTA. Some of those are three years. Many of those go out through the rest of the decade.' The bulk of the targeted over-$3 billion quarter is driven by data center and communications, 'given that that's 80% of our revenue': 800G 'still growing very robustly', 1.6T 'ramping incredibly fast', OCS ramping through the fiscal year, CPO 'starting to really kick in in our December quarter', multi-rail, and pricing improvements, 'either kind of normal pricing improvements or pricing improvements that are part of our LTAs'. On supply: 'Across data center and communications, I am trying to think if there is any product line we are not supply constrained on' — 'we can sell as fast as we can ramp production.'
quarterly_data.figure: LTA pricing set through the length of the LTA (some three years, many to the end of the decade); data center and communications ~80% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — LASER SOURCING MIX, CEO Jim Anderson: 'Today we use a mix of internally produced and externally sourced' lasers for Datacom transceivers; 'over the long term, we'll have some portion of our Datacom transceivers that'll be supported by external sources', for 'a number of strategic reasons', but as internal production grows 'I would expect over time for a greater percentage of our transceivers to be serviced with internal indium phosphide.'

CALL (verbatim) — CPO VERSUS NPO ADOPTION PATH, CEO Jim Anderson: 'Some customers that we're engaged with on NPO, I expect to eventually transfer to CPO further down the line, and some are choosing to go directly to CPO. It really depends on the particular customer and comes down to their specific architecture.' 'Most of these projects are focused on scale-up applications where we're going to be converting more of those copper electrical lines to optical over the coming years', which he called incremental addressable market for Coherent and the optics industry. PhotonLink responds to 'customers not wanting to just buy a point individual ingredient like a laser or an isolator, but really wanting help bringing the full solution'.

CALL (verbatim) — COMMUNICATIONS AND INDUSTRIAL, CEO Jim Anderson: in telecom and DCI 'we actually sell at multiple different levels' — components, subsystems ('amplifiers, line cards') and 'in some cases, we'll sell full systems'; scale-across DCI falls within the communications business, where 'we're going to continue to see faster growth'. Multi-rail: 'Our technology for multi-rail systems is in the hands of customers now. We've sampled that', and 'the demand just continues to go up for anything DCI or scale-across related.' Industrial: 'longer-term opportunities in fusion energy, quantum technologies, and microLED display capital equipment.'

CALL (verbatim) — MARGIN AND COST STRUCTURE, CFO Sherri Luther: gross margin gains, mainly in data center and communications, were 'driven by lower product input costs, improved manufacturing yields and efficiencies, including continued progress on our six-inch indium phosphide platform, as well as benefits from our pricing optimization efforts', and she expects gross margin to keep improving; 'The bulk of the 6-inch indium phosphide product ramp is still ahead of us', as are the 1.6T, OCS, CPO, multi-rail and thermal-management ramps. Opex: Q4 R&D 10.2% of revenue (9.9% in Q3, 9.8% a year earlier) and 9.7% for FY2026 (9.5% in FY2025), focused on transceivers, CPO, OCS systems and thermal management; SG&A 8.2% of revenue in Q4 (9.4%, 10.3%) and 9.2% for FY2026 (10.5%); FY2026 non-GAAP opex $1.35 billion (from $1.17 billion). Shared-services benefits 'exceeded our original expectations' and are expected to increase through FY2027, and 'there is more operating leverage that we will get out of R&D as well.' The capex is 'primarily directed towards advanced tooling and state-of-the-art manufacturing equipment'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 R&D 10.2% and SG&A 8.2% of revenue; FY2026 non-GAAP opex $1.35B (from $1.17B)
